chunks: Indeed, you are only a warner, and for every people is a guide [Quran 13:7].

So he said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) is the warner and Ali is the guide. But, by God, it did not cease to be from us, and will not cease to be among us until the Hour.'

key_terms.السَّاعَةِ: The Hour — the Day of Judgment, marking the end of the world
key_terms.الْهَادِي: The Guide (definite) — specific title applied to Imam Ali as the designated guide for his era
key_terms.مُنْذِرٌ: Warner — the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), who warns humanity of consequences
key_terms.هَادٍ: Guide — Imam Ali (AS) and by extension all the Imams, who guide humanity to truth

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about Quran 13:7 regarding the Prophet as warner and Ali as guide?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) interprets Quran 13:7 by identifying the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) as the warner and Imam Ali (AS) as the guide. He then emphasizes, with an oath by God, that this divinely-appointed role of guidance (wilayah/imamate) has never departed from the Ahl al-Bayt and will remain with them until the Day of Judgment. This hadith was narrated in a context where the Imam was explaining Quranic verses about spiritual authority to his companions, establishing the doctrinal basis of the Imamate.
